WELCOME
New here? Then you have already done the thing this paper is about — you noticed something. What you are looking at is a prototype — the shape of the paper, not a published issue. Some stories are illustrative and the artwork stands in for photographs we do not have yet. The first real issue publishes November 1, 2026. Kindness happens all day, in every neighbourhood, and almost none of it is ever written down. This paper writes it down. Most of what you will read was reported first by a community newspaper or by the organisation doing the work; we carry it, we credit them, and every headline links home to the people who earned it. The Gazette did not perform these acts. It noticed them, and named who did. The rest of the paper belongs to A²OK World — a kindness civilization eleven thousand years old, if you believe our archaeologist — and that half is our own story, always labelled as such, never mixed in with the news. Read anything. Then tell us what we missed, because kindness is an annual plant: if the seed does not go in the ground every year, it disappears. — The Editors

The Lead · World News

Strangers. Seven hours. One 90th birthday.

Sometimes kindness does not require knowing someone. It requires deciding they are worth the detour.

Carried by the Gazette  ·  Reported by The Washington Post · Aug. 18, 2026

KELOWNA, B.C. — Wildfire smoke over Western Canada forced Patricia Robinson's flight to turn back mid-air, stranding her hours from a celebration her family had spent months arranging. Two passengers she had met that morning rented a car and drove her roughly seven hours so that she would not miss her ninetieth birthday.

Neither of them knew her before that day. Neither asked for anything. The story reached international coverage only because a family member wrote about it afterwards — which is to say it very nearly was not a story at all.

Speaking A²OK · Key Concept

The Ripple

Not a nice coincidence. A documented transmission — one act or story provably inspiring another. We only claim one when somebody says so in their own words.

Ripple Confirmed
They said outright what inspired them.
Ripple Identified
Strong evidence, short of a direct statement.
Possible Ripple
Plausible. Not established. Marked as such.
Ripple Lost
The trail ends in anonymity. Often the best ending.

Ripple Identified · Chain of 2 · March, Cambridgeshire

The ripple that started with an unkindness

Somebody posted a public complaint about a neighbour's overgrown garden. A stranger read it, went round, and cut the grass for nothing. He now does three gardens a week.

Gazette original  ·  Confirmed against BBC News and the subject's own account

MARCH, ENGLAND — The Gazette went looking for whatever inspired Stephen Jalland, a handyman clearing overgrown gardens at no charge. The answer was not what we expected. It was a critical Facebook post — someone complaining, publicly, about how a neighbour's garden looked. Jalland read it and, instead of joining in, went and cut the garden himself.

We are still working backwards. We do not know who wrote the original post and we may never — which would make this a Ripple Lost, an honest ending and by no means the worst one.

Real archaeology · Dmanisi, Georgia

Did humans invent kindness 1.8 million years ago?

An ancient skull may say something about one of humanity's oldest technologies: caring for someone who could no longer care for themselves.

The find is genuine, published and not ours. What the Gazette adds is the question: if a group kept an aging member alive who could no longer feed himself, is kindness older than agriculture, older than language, older than everything we usually credit for civilization?

A²OK World Editorial · Opinion

We don't compete. We multiply.

There are at least seventy organisations doing this work, and not one of them keeps a record of the others. Every counter in the field counts only its own users — because in every case the number is the credential.

We can hold the record precisely because nobody here has a name attached to it. No founder profile grows. No résumé is built. If another organisation generates more kindness than we do this year, we will report it on our own front page, cheerfully, and mean it.

Society is not running out of compassion. Millions of people hold doors, fix cars for nothing and feed strangers without ever filing a press release. The world is simply very good at overlooking it.

Kindness is an annual plant. If the seeds are not planted every year it disappears, and somebody has to go and find new seed. That is the whole reason this paper exists.

A²OK World · Philosophy

Every headline in this section is drawn from a published source, and source links are provided where available. Some publishers block automated verification; those stories carry a human review pending mark and do not run until an editor has confirmed them directly. That is the whole proposition when we call an editor: we are not asking for their coverage — we have been carrying it, with their byline attached, and sending readers back. Four papers are absent only because their sites blocked automated reading: the Midway Como Monitor and MyVillager among them.  ·  Southside Pride ran its farewell edition on December 2, 2025. Its archive is still live and worth carrying — and its 14,000-copy South Minneapolis footprint is now empty.
